title: Trust AI Agents to Act: Start With Your Data Foundation
summary: AI agents are moving from answering questions to taking action. Learn how a governed data foundation and an agentic control plane help enterprises scale AI.
body_markdown:
For the past two years, most enterprises have used AI to answer questions. But that’s changing fast. AI agents are now resolving support tickets, reconciling accounts and helping teams prep for sales calls — all with limited human involvement. The question is no longer whether AI can do the work. It’s whether organizations can trust AI to do the work.


That trust doesn’t come from a model. It comes from the data that agents reason over and the rules that govern what they’re allowed to do.


The organizations pulling ahead are not the ones with the most agents. They’re the ones with a strong data foundation underneath them.


## From answers to action: A new operating model for enterprise AI


Today’s AI agents monitor, reason and execute across systems. They can turn insight into multistep action without waiting for a human to bridge every gap. That’s a fundamentally different job than answering a question, and it raises the stakes. A wrong answer can be ignored. A wrong action has consequences.


This is why the most effective organizations treat governance as a design principle, not an add-on. They onboard agents the way they onboard employees. Each agent gets an identity and a defined role with scoped access to data and regular performance reviews.


Role-based access controls and policy enforcement apply to agents as they do to people. The result is a system where leaders can expand what agents do with confidence because every new agent, workflow and use case builds on the same trusted, governed enterprise data.


## The agentic control plane: How AI agents can work together safely


Agents will continue to come from everywhere: internal teams, third-party vendors and startups that don’t exist yet. Open standards like Model Context Protocol (MCP) for agent-to-tool communication and Agent2Agent (A2A) for agent-to-agent communication make that diversity a strength. No enterprise will likely want a single monolithic AI system. Instead, they’ll assemble the best agent for each job.


What keeps a multiagent ecosystem productive and safe is an agentic control plane. It’s the coordination layer that connects enterprise data, intelligence and action within a single governance boundary. Before any agent acts, the control plane should answer three questions:


- **Should this action happen?**
- **Which policy does it fall under?**
- **When does a human need to step in?**


In short, the control plane translates what AI can do into what the organization has authorized it to do. It’s the difference between a compelling pilot and a production system leaders can trust.


## AI agents in production: What changes for finance, sales and marketing


The most immediate impact shows up in how people work with their own data. Employees ask complex questions in natural language and get reliable, cited answers, often without a help ticket, a dashboard or a queue for the data team.


- **Finance** teams forecast revenue, run scenarios and automate reconciliation through conversations, with answer citing the tables and queries behind it.
- **Sales** teams surface pipeline risk, prep for customer meetings and uncover cross-sell opportunities in minutes rather than hours.
- **Marketing** teams detect performance shifts as they happen, then adjust campaigns and spend in near real time.


## A clear path to the agentic enterprise


Most organizations are already on this path. The ebook,["Understanding the Agentic Enterprise Era: How Leading Organizations Are Mobilizing the AI Advantage,"](https://www.snowflake.com/en/resources/ebook/understanding-the-agentic-enterprise-era-how-leading-organizations-are-mobilizing-the-ai-advantage/) maps it in three stages:


- **Baseline curiosity:** Exploring tools and building stakeholder alignment
- **Contextual insight:** Investing in the data infrastructure that makes AI trustworthy at scale
- **Autonomous, policy-driven action:** Running full agentic operations with governance, human oversight and a control plane coordinating it all


Each stage builds on the last. An organization can’t skip to autonomous action without the trusted data and governance that makes it safe. The organizations that start deliberately, with a strong data strategy, governance framework from day one and a control plane built for a multivendor agent ecosystem, are the ones turning today’s experiments into lasting competitive advantage.
